There is, however, meaningful pair-specific instructional coherence: two complementary visual-perception strategies deliberately taught in consecutive Grade R terms under one sub-strand, each reinforcing the use of visual and pictorial cues to make meaning. That supports canonical relatesTo (symmetric, direction null, canonical endpoint order preserved) rather than buildsTowards or no_relation. Direction is lower-to-higher grade rank (Grade 2 to Grade 3), which is the only permitted buildsTowards direction here. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 2 (rank 2) but in different Skill Areas: the first is Term 3 WRITING / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' ('Uses correct punctuation (full stops, commas, question marks and exclamation marks) so that others can read what has been written'); the second is Term 4 LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL) / 'Daily / Weekly activities' ('Uses terms such as noun, adjective, verb, pronoun, preposition, comma, question mark, paragraph when talking about own writing'). There is genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence: both concern punctuation marks (comma, question mark) in the learner's own writing, with one covering accurate written production and the other oral metalinguistic reflection on that writing, so each meaningfully reinforces the other. However, the second is not a deepening or extension of the first: its substance is grammar metalanguage (word classes, paragraphing) delivered orally, and proficiency in placing punctuation correctly does not specifically raise the likelihood of success in naming nouns, verbs, pronouns or prepositions when talking about writing. The nomination evidence is weak surface similarity (LC tag Jaccard 0.077 on 'writing'; text-token Jaccard 0.057 on 'question'/'uses'; shared Grade ancestor only), which cannot by itself license developmental dependency. Canonical relatesTo (symmetric, null direction) is therefore the correct judgment rather than buildsTowards or no_relation. Material limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, so this judgment rests on the bounded excerpt.

The first is Term 2 / WRITING / Shared, Group and Independent Writing: 'Participates in a discussion to choose a topic to write about', where discussion functions narrowly as a pre-writing step for topic selection. The second is Term 4 / LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL) / Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities: 'Participates in discussions, suggesting topics for discussion and asking questions for information and reporting back on the group's work', with LCs 'Suggests topics for discussion', 'Asks questions for information' and 'Reports back on the group's work'. There is genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence: discussion participation and topic-generation skills are exercised in both, one in service of writing and one as a focussed oral competence, so each meaningfully reinforces the other across strands. Symmetric relatesTo in unchanged canonical endpoint order is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs carry the identical printed CAPS statement 'Makes links to own experience when reading with the teacher, viewing television or pictures' and share the single Learning Component 122fb376 (token/trigram Jaccard 1.0). They differ only in Term scope within the same Grade R, Skill Area EMERGENT READING, Sub-strand Shared Reading: the first is Grade R Term 3 (window 8, page 49), the second Grade R Term 4 (window 11, page 54). The bounded evidence shows no expanded capability in Term 4 (no added text length, text types, letter range, or increased independence), so a developmental buildsTowards from Term 3 to Term 4 is not substantively supported; it is CAPS's deliberate term-to-term continuation of the same shared-reading personal-connection skill. That continuation is pair-specific and instructionally coherent (same sub-strand, consecutive terms, same single LC), which exceeds mere generic word overlap, so a symmetric relatesTo is the appropriate judgment. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the absence of any qualifying expansion in the full printed bullets cannot be fully confirmed from this excerpt.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R, Term 1, Listening and Speaking (Oral) skills under the same sub-strand 'Daily activities in all areas of Language and other subjects' and the same source table row/page. 'Listens to and repeats rhythmic patterns (clap, clap-clap, clap) and copies correctly' and 'Sings simple songs and does actions (with help)' are complementary oral/auditory imitation activities: both require attending to an auditory model and reproducing it, one through rhythmic clapping, the other through song plus accompanying actions. Their Learning Components (listens to/repeats rhythmic patterns; sings simple songs/does actions with help) show genuine conceptual coherence in auditory attention and imitation, but neither statement is scoped as more complex or more independent than the other (the song item is still 'with help'), and they sit at the same Grade R rank and same Term, so no substantive evidence supports a developmental direction either way. Shared ancestry, page proximity and the trivial token overlap ('and', 'e', 'g', 'to') add no semantic weight on their own. relatesTo captures the reinforcement without asserting dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R, Term 1 Skills printed as sibling bullets in the same Listening and Speaking (Oral) sub-strand 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning' (same page/table row, identical identity scope and rank 0). The first ('Plays games such as ‘Where is it?’ finding an object hidden in a classroom among other items') exercises visual search plus oral instruction-following; the second ('Arranges a set of three pictures ... logical sequence of events when verbalised and relates the story created') exercises picture sequencing and oral narration, with LCs tagged sequencing/story/retelling. They are complementary applications of visual/pictorial meaning-making that reinforce one another, but neither statement's capability is evidenced as supporting success in the other: the hidden-object game does not supply the narrative sequencing demand, and sequencing does not depend on object-location games. Token/trigram overlap is only on function words ('a', 'in', 'such'), and shared parent, same term and page proximity alone are not developmental evidence, so a same-term directional buildsTowards is unwarranted. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge/audit context, so judgment rests on the printed statement text and LCs available here.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit under Grade 3 (rank 3), with the first in Term 1 (Reading and Phonics / Phonics sub-strand: 'Writes three short sentences dictated by teacher', LC tags dictation, phonics, sentences, writing) and the second in Term 2 (Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing: 'Reads and edits own writing by correcting spelling, punctuation, etc.', LCs 'Reads own writing' and 'Edits own writing by correcting spelling, punctuation, etc.'). Direction Term 1 to Term 2 within the same grade is permitted. Dictation writing establishes accurate sound-to-spelling transcription and sentence-level conventions (capitals, full stops) under teacher control; that transcription and convention accuracy plausibly supports the more independent and metacognitive task of rereading and self-correcting spelling and punctuation in one's own composed writing. This is a supportive developmental link, not a shared-parent or wording artefact (token overlap was trivial: 'by', 'writing'), so confidence is moderate rather than high; source evidence for both endpoints is truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Term 3, Skill Area 'Emergent Reading', but under different Sub-strands: the first ('Understands that words consist of more than one sound... 'hand' has four sounds h-a-n-d') is a phonemic-awareness statement under 'Relates sounds to letters and words', while the second (''Reads' high frequency words in the community: road signs, shop names') is an environmental-print/whole-word recognition statement under 'Emergent reading skills' (LC tags: environmental print, high frequency words, signs). They are coherent, complementary emergent word-level reading skills that reinforce each other within the same term, but the evidence shows no substantive deepening, extension, or dependency in either direction: recognising logographic community print does not require phoneme segmentation, and segmenting spoken words is not presented as an extension of sign reading. Same-rank, same-term placement alone cannot supply developmental direction, and the only token overlap is the generic word 'words' plus weak page proximity, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so the full source text was not available.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the same Grade R (rank 0), Term 4, EMERGENT READING table cell, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Emergent reading skills' ('Reads' picture books of increasing complexity) and 'Independent Reading' ('Reads' books independently for pleasure in the library or classroom reading corner, turning the pages correctly, showing respect for books). They are substantively coherent — both are emergent 'reading' of books, with LC overlap on books/reading — and they reinforce each other: engaging with increasingly complex picture books and choosing books independently for pleasure with correct book handling and respect. However, they are concurrent Term 4 expectations with different emphases (text complexity vs. independence, book-handling conventions and attitude), and the bounded evidence (truncated source evidence for both endpoints and truncated LC evidence for the second) gives no substantive basis for a same-rank, same-term developmental direction in either orientation. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.
